problem: "Tasklets are built on softirqs, one instance per CPU" reads as if one copy of a tasklet exists per CPU and they run in parallel. The standard rule is the opposite: a given tasklet never runs on two CPUs at the same time, so it needs no locking against itself.
fix: "Tasklets are built on softirqs, but a given tasklet runs on only one CPU at a time, so it never races with itself; it still cannot sleep."

problem: "It reports an event and carries no data" is true only for the standard signals. A signal sent with sigqueue() carries a value and a siginfo_t, and real-time signals are queued with such data.
fix: Add: "Standard signals carry no data; a signal sent with sigqueue() (or a real-time signal) can carry a small value."

problem: "It takes pending & ~blocked, clears that bit" does not say what happens when several signals are pending; a student may assume order is arbitrary or arrival order.
fix: Add: "If several are pending, Linux delivers the lowest-numbered signal first, so signal 9 is handled before signal 15."

problem: The edge chain top half → softirq/tasklet → workqueue suggests a workqueue always follows a softirq. The prose correctly says "softirqs, tasklets or workqueues"; the figure shows them as consecutive stages.
fix: Show softirq/tasklet and workqueue as two parallel outputs from the top half, not as one chain, so the figure matches "or".
